rationale: Both follow the same find-the-cluster-then-adjust-for-qu approach with helpful rule comments. B splits the input with text.split(), so repeated or surrounding whitespace is handled. A's split(' ') yields empty strings in that case, and word[0] then raises IndexError. B also names the vowel set as a constant. B has blemishes too. Its elif branch for 'qu' can never fire, because the scan stops on a vowel and never on a 'q', so that branch is dead code. Its word[i] access could fail for an all-consonant word ending in 'q'. A's for/else and slice-based 'qu' check are neat, idiomatic Python. On balance B's handling of real-world whitespace and its named constant make it slightly more robust, though neither is clearly superior.
